s: Global topic-based publish/subscribe fanning events out to independent subscriptions with per-key ordering options.
w: Publishers emit to topics; each subscription receives the full stream independently (queue or streaming pull). Ordering keys serialize per-key when chosen. Exactly-once delivery feature exists regionally now. Backlogs persist until acked/dead-lettered; snapshotting preserves offsets during migrations.
use: Event broadcast to many services (order.created -> email, analytics, fraud)
Ingest front door feeding stream processors and warehouses simultaneously
Microservices choreography replacing brittle HTTP chains
avoid: Simple worker-queue semantics where sqs-style polling fits cheaper
Very long retention/replay years back (kinesis/warehouse tiers better)

pat.d: Services react to each other's published facts; no central orchestrator.

pits: Subscriber slowdowns grow unbounded backlog - alarm on oldest-unacked age
tips: Contrast queue (competing consumers, one winner) vs topic fan-out (everyone gets a copy) explicitly
